newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Queensland revamps gaming regime.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Queensland revamps gaming regime.

text.p: Queensland State Deputy Premier Joan Sheldon said on Wednesday the state government had agreed with clubs and hotels on new arrangements governing the use and taxation of gaming machines in the state.
"Under the agreeement signed by all major parties, clubs and hotels will receive an increase in funds from gaming machines through cuts in government taxation," Sheldon said in a statement.
There would be a corresponding increase in the numbers of gaming machines, which would be staggered over several years, said David Watson, Sheldon's parliamentary secretary.
The government intended to opt out of owning gaming machines, Sheldon and Watson said.
"Hotels and clubs will have the ability to purchase the gaming machine of their choice, either from a licensed operator or the Queensland Office of Gaming regulation," the said.
"Sites will be given the opportunity to buy their existing gaming machine stock."
Licensed operators would take over the monitoring of sites from the Queensland Office of Gaming regulation.
"Unlike the arrangements in other states, the licensed operator will be restricted to 40 percent of the market share."
The right to own machines would remain with the hotels and clubs at all times and they would be able to seek finance to buy the machines from licensed financiers such as banks.
While it would be mandatory for hotels and clubs to join up with a licensed operator for monitoring purposes with a maximum price set by the government, no site would be forced to buy extra services.
"In order to maintain industry integrity, direct selling from machine manufacturers to clubs and hotels will not be permitted."
"Hotels and clubs will only be allowed to purchase gaming machines through a licensed operator."
The leading manufacturers of gaming machines for sale in Australia are Bally Entertainment Corp of the United States, now owned by Hilton Hotels Corp, Aristocrat Leisure Ltd and AWA Ltd.
